segments.text: What if Luffy never ate a Devil Fruit? Same pirate dream. Dramatically fewer elastic escape plans.
segments.label: NO RUBBER STILL LOUD

segments.text: In this timeline, Shanks keeps the fruit away. Somebody finally installed childproofing on the plot.
segments.label: ONE STOLEN SNACK CHANGES THINGS

segments.text: Luffy keeps swimming. Useful, honestly. Revolutionary technology called not immediately drowning after you leave.
segments.label: SWIMMING IS BACK

segments.text: But his body isn't rubber. Bullets won't bounce because he's built different. Be serious.
segments.label: THE PUNCH PROBLEM

segments.text: He needs different training, defense, and discipline. Shanks isn't issuing a victory certificate.
segments.label: A DIFFERENT TRAINING PATH

segments.text: The crew matters more. Zoro covers combat while somebody explains that cannons aren't just motivational obstacles.
segments.label: THE CREW IS NOT OPTIONAL

segments.text: Luffy still leaps toward danger. We removed the fruit, not his adventurous single brain cell.
segments.label: THE SAME AWFUL INSTINCTS

segments.text: Positioning and tools become essential. A rope extends your reach without a supernatural childhood accident.
segments.label: BORROW A TOOL BRO

segments.text: Then a crewmate falls overboard. Luffy can finally help instead of becoming the second rescue objective.
segments.label: THE RESCUE REVERSAL

segments.text: The trade? Extraordinary flexibility disappears, but an ordinary ability changes how he protects friends.
segments.label: POWER IS NOT PERSONALITY

segments.text: Some battles become harder or unwinnable. Plot armor isn't a documented training program. Please show your sources.
segments.label: NO FREE WIN STAMP

segments.text: The dream survives. The crew matters more. And the captain's relationship with water stops being legally binding beef.
segments.label: THE DREAM SURVIVES
